subject: Request: EU failover latency boundary + DR carveout for Crestline
messages:
From: Mike Lang <mike.lang@crestline-payments.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@crestline-payments.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 14:12:00 +00:00
Subject: EU failover ask — latency boundary and temporary RTO/RPO exception

Jonas,

Thanks again for last week's demo. We like Redwood's regional routing and warm-standby story, but our procurement and ops teams flagged a gap in the EU failover SLA language that will block final approval. Two asks from our side:

1) We need a formal exception for the "latency boundary" during cross-region switchover. Crestline will accept a 2-hour soft switchover window for non-critical routing (affects <10% of traffic) during the first 6 months of go-live.

2) Because we replicate certain stateful artifacts externally for analytics, we need the target RTO to be extended to 2 hours and the RPO to 15 minutes during the standby activation window for eu-central. This is a carveout to your standard 30m RTO / 60s RPO.

Attached is a short note from our infra team (crestline_failover_request.docx) and a simple diagram. Can Redwood confirm whether you can sign an SLA exception letter or suggest compensating controls (e.g., longer warm-standby readiness tests, retained packet logs, advance notice windows)?

We'd prefer a written exception in the form of an addendum that we can attach to the purchase order.

Regards,
Mike Lang
Director, Infrastructure
Crestline Payments

Attachment: crestline_failover_request.docx (docx)
Attachment: architecture_eu_warm-standby.png (png)

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: mike.lang@crestline-payments.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: EU failover ask — latency boundary and temporary RTO/RPO exception

Team — forwarding Crestline's request. High level: they want a temporary carveout for eu-central (2h RTO / 15m RPO) for a subset of traffic with an official addendum. They called out a "latency boundary" acceptance for non-critical routing during first 6 months.

Can you each assess:
- Laura: operational impact — can we meet the exception via warm-standby + extended holdback, any monitoring/trace implications, how to word the addendum so it's low-friction?
- Evelyn: compliance/legal flags (cross-border transfer, auditability), required mitigations.

Also include a proposed fallback timeline (testing cadence, readiness checks) and whether we should condition the exception on a commercial term (e.g., 12-month commitment or higher TCV). I copied Mike so they're aware we'll follow up.

Thanks,
Jonas

--- Original message attached for context ---

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, mike.lang@crestline-payments.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EU failover ask — latency boundary and temporary RTO/RPO exception

Jonas / Mike — quick ops assessment below. TL;DR: we can support a scoped exception with conditions.

Operational notes:
- Warm-standby model: we can keep eu-central warm with reduced replicas and prefix caching. For the first 6 months we accept a 2-hour service-level activation window for a subset of traffic (<=10%) provided Crestline agrees to two compensations:
  * Daily readiness probe results (automated report) during the first 30 days; weekly thereafter for the remainder of the 6 months.
  * A runbook-triggered KV-cache reseed procedure that Crestline must permit during failover drills (we can automate this).

- RPO/RTO: raising RTO to 2 hours and RPO to 15 minutes for specified routes is achievable if we change the replication snapshot cadence and add a short-lived write-buffering layer (we already support this pattern). There will be a measurable hit to recovery cost and a small increase in failover latency during the window.

- Suggested SLA addendum language (summary):
  * "Redwood will support an exception to standard Failover RTO/RPO for the eu-central region limited to the production routes listed in Appendix A. Exception duration: 6 months from go-live unless otherwise extended by written agreement. Conditions: daily readiness reporting, mutually-agreed failover drills, and advance 30-minute activation notice."

- Commercial conditioning: Ops recommends gating the exception on a 12-month committed reserved capacity plan (Redwood Dedicated or a higher-tier hosted commit) to offset the added operational cost.

I'm attaching a PDF redline of the SLA addendum (redline_sla_carveout_v1.pdf) with suggested wording and an appendix template. If ok, we should propose a one-page addendum that Legal approves and then present it to Crestline.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redline_sla_carveout_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: mike.lang@crestline-payments.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: EU failover ask — latency boundary and temporary RTO/RPO exception

Thanks — a few compliance points before we issue an addendum:

1) Data residency & transfers: Any exception that changes replication or buffering behavior must be explicit about the categories of data involved. Crestline must confirm no regulated PII flows through the temporary buffering layer. If regulated data is involved, we need either a) controller-to-processor clause permitting transient buffer transfers, or b) an on-premise alternative.

2) Auditability: We should require that Redwood provide preserved audit logs for the exception period (retention 12 months) and an access pattern for audits.

3) Security controls: enable HSM-based key wrapping for cross-region replication and a mandatory pre-failover checklist (signed by Crestline's Ops lead) for any unscheduled switchover during the exception window.

If Crestline agrees to these controls, Legal is comfortable with a 6-month exception. We should also include an auto-revert clause: if a compliance violation or data incident occurs during the carveout period, the exception terminates immediately and Redwood will restore baseline RTO/RPO processes.

I'll draft the legal block and send a redline.

—Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Mike Lang <mike.lang@crestline-payments.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, procure@crestline-payments.com
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 16:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: EU failover ask — latency boundary and temporary RTO/RPO exception

Mike — thanks for the clear ask and for being flexible on scope. Proposal next steps:

1) Redwood will produce a one-page SLA addendum (ops + legal redline) that captures: exception scope (routes in Appendix A), 6-month duration, RTO 2h / RPO 15m for the scope, daily readiness reporting for first 30 days, audit log retention 12 months, HSM key-wrapping for cross-region replication, and an auto-revert clause.

2) Commercial: we propose conditioning the exception on a 12-month capacity commitment (suggested uplift: 20% committed capacity over baseline) to cover operational overhead. This is negotiable — happy to align with procurement.

3) I'll schedule a 30-minute call next week to walk through Appendix A and the draft addendum. Please pick a time here: https://cal.redwood.com/jonas_weber/30min (or reply with availability).

If that works, we'll send the draft addendum and a short checklist for Crestline to confirm (no-regulated-PII statement + Ops signoff).

Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
